question: Why must GPS satellite clocks be corrected for Einstein's relativity?
answer: Einstein's special and general relativity say time passes at a different rate on the satellites than on Earth. Left alone, the satellites' atomic clocks slip out of step with ours and GPS loses accuracy. So the clocks get slight corrections.
move: In orbit time runs at a different pace, so GPS clocks are corrected.

web.label: Two clocks side by side: one on Earth and one on the right that you drag up into orbit. Watch both clocks run, then apply Einstein's correction to see whether they stay in step.
